title: Mapping
description:
How a file's columns are read: the header's line, the separator, and what each column holds.
[`mapping`] returns the one the header states; a caller may change it and read the file by it
with [`read_with`].

clock.description: The clock's column, from 0. Its [`ColumnMapping::unit`] must be a unit of time.

clock_wrap.description:
The count the clock turns over at, in its unit, for a logger's counter that runs over,
such as 2³² microseconds; `None` for a clock that doesn't (module docs, *A column
mapping*).

columns.description: Every column, in the file's order.

decimal_comma.description:
Whether a comma in a cell is the decimal mark, as `1,5` for 1.5; only where the separator
isn't a comma. Either way, a cell in the other mark is no number (module docs, *Rows*).

header_line.description:
The header row's line, from 1; `None` for a file with no header row, whose rows start at
its first line that isn't blank or a `#` comment.

primary.description:
The primary track's column, from 0: the barometric altitude above the pad, which becomes
[`FlightLog::altitude_m`] on the clock, [`FlightLog::time_s`] (module docs, *The record*).
Its quantity must be [`Quantity::AltitudeAboveGround`]. `None` for a table that has none,
or doesn't say which; the header never says, so [`mapping`] returns `None`.

rows.description: How each row is written: plain cells, unless the mapping says otherwise.

name.description: The column's name, as the header writes it, or as the caller names it.

quantity.description:
What the column measures; `None` to keep its numbers as written
([`Quantity::Unrecognized`]). Ignored for the clock.

skip.description:
Whether the mapping leaves the column out, as cells beside a table that aren't part of it:
no channel is made of it, its cells only counted in the row's width.

unit.description:
The unit the values are written in, one of [`unit_spellings`], such as `ft` or
`m/s^2`, in any case; `None` when [`ColumnMapping::quantity`] is `None` or
[`Quantity::Number`].

Quantity.description:
What a channel measures. The unit is SI but for angles, which are in degrees as GNSS
receivers and loggers write them.

oneOf.description:
A barometric altitude above the logger's own zero, m; in a Featherweight GPS tracker's
summary ([`LogFormat::FeatherweightSummaryCsv`]), its receiver's altitude above the pad it
states.
A barometric altitude above mean sea level, m.
An altitude from GNSS, above mean sea level as the receiver states it, m.
An altitude the logger integrated from its accelerometer, above its zero, m.

An altitude whose sensor or zero the file doesn't state, m: a table read by its header
([`LogFormat::GenericTable`]) names an altitude and its unit, and often no more.
Air pressure, Pa.

A speed or velocity the logger computed, m/s; its column says from which sensor and along
which direction.
An acceleration, m/s²; its column says along which axis, and whether gravity is in it.
A temperature, K.
An electric potential, V, such as a battery's or a pyro channel's.
An electric current, A.
A latitude, degrees north.
A longitude, degrees east.
An angle, degrees, such as a tilt or a bearing.
A rate of turn, degrees per second, such as a gyroscope's about one of its axes.
A distance, m, such as a GNSS receiver's range from the pad.

A time of day on the logger's own clock, s after its midnight, in whatever time zone the
clock was set to: files state none.
A length of time, s, such as a summary's time from liftoff to an event.

A number with no unit, such as a count of satellites, a signal strength, a flag or a
state code, as the file writes it, or a fraction, such as a percentage the file writes,
divided by 100.

A column HPR Sim doesn't know: its values as the file writes them, in a unit HPR Sim
doesn't know either.

RowForm.description: How a table's rows are written (module docs, *A column mapping*).

oneOf.description: Cells between separators.
A list between `[` and `]`, as a program printing its lists writes it: `[1, 2.5, True]`.

A date and time, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` with any fraction of a second, then `:` and the
cells, between parentheses if they are a tuple, as `(x, y, z)`. The stamp is column 0, the
clock, in seconds.
